Raw deliverable below. Anchors (ML348/ML349) are given as PubChem-fetch commands rather than hand-typed SMILES on purpose — see note — because a mistyped anchor silently invalidates the docking method-validation, and they are method-validation only (d_novel_only), not campaign output.

---

## 1. LIGAND SET (SMILES, copy-pasteable)

```
# === ANCHORS (neutral baselines · method-validation only · NOT campaign output) ===
# Do NOT trust a hand-typed anchor SMILES. Fetch canonical from PubChem by name at prep time:
#   ML349 (APT2/LYPLA2 ref, the 5SYN co-crystal ligand)  -> PubChem name "ML349"
#   ML348 (APT1/LYPLA1 ref)                               -> PubChem name "ML348"
# curl -s "https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/rest/pug/compound/name/ML349/property/CanonicalSMILES,IsomericSMILES/TXT"
# curl -s "https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/rest/pug/compound/name/ML348/property/CanonicalSMILES,IsomericSMILES/TXT"
# The docked ML349 pose MUST reproduce the 5SYN crystal pose (RMSD < 2 Å) before any novel score is trusted.

# === WARHEAD REFERENCE (neutral · ML349-class 2-acylaminothiophene-3-carboxylate scaffold) ===
W0    CCOC(=O)c1ccsc1NC(=O)Cc1ccccc1

# === NOVEL SERIES: neutral warhead + solvent-exposed cationic exit-vector on para of the phenylacetyl ring ===
# (para position of the acyl aryl ring is the solvent-facing exit vector per Step-3 pose reasoning)
N1    CCOC(=O)c1ccsc1NC(=O)Cc1ccc(OCC[NH+](C)C)cc1
N2    CCOC(=O)c1ccsc1NC(=O)Cc1ccc(OCCC[NH+](C)C)cc1
N3    CCOC(=O)c1ccsc1NC(=O)Cc1ccc(C[NH+]2CCCC2)cc1
N4    CCOC(=O)c1ccsc1NC(=O)Cc1ccc(OCC[NH+]2CCCC2)cc1
N5    CCOC(=O)c1ccsc1NC(=O)Cc1ccc(OCC[NH+]2CCOCC2)cc1
N6    CCOC(=O)c1ccsc1NC(=O)Cc1ccc(OCCNC(=[NH2+])N)cc1
N7    CCOC(=O)c1ccsc1NC(=O)Cc1ccc(OCCN2CC[NH+](C)CC2)cc1
N8    CCOC(=O)c1ccsc1NC(=O)Cc1ccc(OCC[NH2+]CCC[NH3+])cc1
N9    CCOC(=O)c1ccsc1NC(=O)Cc1ccc(OCC[NH+]2CC[NH2+]CC2)cc1
N10   CCOC(=O)c1ccsc1NC(=O)Cc1ccc(OCCCNC(=[NH2+])N)cc1

# === NEGATIVE CONTROLS (expected to FAIL — gate sanity check) ===
NC1   CCOC(=O)c1ccsc1NC(=O)C[N+](C)(C)C
NC2   [NH+](C)(C)CCOc1ccc(CC(=O)O)cc1
```

Notes on the series axes: linker length spans 1–3 heavy atoms (N3 benzylic → N2/N10 propyl-ether); amine type spans tertiary dimethylamino (N1/N2), cyclic pyrrolidinium (N3/N4), morpholinium (N5), N-methylpiperazinium (N7), guanidinium (N6/N10), and doubly-basic +2 (N8 spermidine-like, N9 diprotonated piperazine). NC1 buries a quaternary ammonium **inside** the acyl pocket (cation in hydrophobic channel → affinity collapse). NC2 has the cationic tail but **no warhead** (no thiophene ester to occupy the Ser-His-Asp acyl site → no pocket engagement).

| N1 | +1 | 377 | 2.4 | ✓ |

## 3. Docking protocol — smina vs 5SYN

**Receptor prep**
1. `wget https://files.rcsb.org/download/5SYN.pdb`
2. Note the ML349 HET code and its atom coordinates (centroid = box center); also confirm the catalytic Ser-His-Asp triad residue numbers in 5SYN (APT2/LYPLA2; verify the Ser nucleophile in the SEQRES/SITE records — do not assume numbering).
3. Strip ligand + solvent, keep protein + triad:
   `grep -E "^ATOM" 5SYN.pdb > receptor_raw.pdb` (drops HETATM: ML349, HOH, glycerol, ions). If a structural metal/cofactor sits in the site, keep it; APT2 has none catalytically.
4. Single chain: keep chain A only (`awk '$1=="ATOM" && substr($0,22,1)=="A"'`).
5. Protonate + convert: `obabel receptor_raw.pdb -O receptor.pdbqt -xr -p 7.4` (`-xr` = rigid receptor, adds polar H). Sanity-check the catalytic Ser OG and His are present.

**Ligand prep** (per SMILES)
`obabel -:"<SMILES>" --gen3d -p 7.4 -O lig.pdbqt` — `-p 7.4` respects the explicit charges already in the SMILES; verify formal charge survived (`grep "Total charge" ` / check pdbqt).

**Box**
- Center = ML349 crystal centroid (extract ML349 to `ml349.pdb`, use `smina --autobox_ligand ml349.pdb --autobox_add 10`). The `+10 Å` pad is deliberately generous so the cationic exit-vector can extend toward solvent rather than being forced into the pocket.
- Equivalent explicit box: 22 Å cube on the centroid.
- `--exhaustiveness 32` (novel flexible tails need it), `--num_modes 20`, `--seed 0`.

**Read the score**
- smina reports `Affinity (kcal/mol)`, Vina-type; more negative = tighter. Take mode 1 (top).
- **Validate first:** re-dock ML349 into prepped receptor; require top-pose RMSD < 2 Å vs crystal and affinity in a sane range (≈ −8 to −10). If ML349 doesn't reproduce, the prep is wrong — fix before scoring novels.
- Inspect the winning novel poses: warhead must sit in the acyl channel over Ser; the cation must point **out** to solvent (visual/contact check). A pose that buries the cation is a false positive even with a good number.

**MM-GBSA rescore**
- True MM-GBSA needs OpenMM or Amber (implicit-solvent MM) — **not available from rdkit+smina+openbabel alone.** State this honestly.
- Free-tier proxy on this stack:
  1. `smina --local_only --minimize -r receptor.pdbqt -l docked_pose.pdbqt` → minimized (clash-relaxed) affinity.
  2. Ligand strain = E(bound conformer) − E(global-min conformer), both via rdkit MMFF94: `AllChem.MMFFOptimizeMolecule` + `MMFFGetMoleculeForceField(...).CalcEnergy()`; embed ~50 confs for the global min.
  3. Report **minimized affinity + strain penalty** as the proxy score.
- Caveat (state it): this proxy neglects explicit desolvation of the exit-vector cation and configurational entropy, so it will **overestimate** the value of high-charge (+2) ligands whose desolvation cost is real. The cation is what carries the delta but also what a gas-phase/implicit-poor score mishandles.
- **Honest upgrade path (recommended, free):** run real MM-GBSA on `summer` (RTX 5070 + `fep` conda env / OpenMM already provisioned per project setup) — OpenMM implicit-solvent GBSA or Amber MMPBSA.py on the top 3 poses. Do this before any discovery claim.

## 4. Step-4 pass gate (operational) + pre-docking prior

Gate = **smina top-mode affinity ≤ −8.0 kcal/mol** (proxy for relaxed A_ext ≥ 0.48 potency) **AND predicted delta ≥ 0.772** (satisfied by net charge +1..+2). Both required.

- Delta arm: passed by all +1/+2 (N1–N10, and by-design NC1/NC2). Failed by W0 (neutral) and any species that ends up neutral (watch N5).
- Affinity arm: the discriminator. Novels must keep the ML349-class warhead engaged while the tail exits.

**Predicted to pass BOTH pre-docking (my prior, strongest → weaker):**
1. **N1, N2** — clean +1, short ether-dimethylamino, minimal warhead perturbation, logP mid-window. Highest confidence.
2. **N4, N10** — +1, pyrrolidinium / propyl-guanidinium; slightly larger but exit-vector geometry favorable.
3. **N7** — +1, MW 432 (still <500), piperazine solvating well.
4. **N6** — +1 guanidinium; best GAG-avidity (delta-strong) but logP 1.3 near lower edge.
5. **N3** — +1 but benzylic amine sits closest to pocket mouth → mild risk of cation partially buried (affinity risk).

**Predicted delta-pass but affinity-marginal:** N8, N9 (+2, logP ≤1.0 — desolvation penalty, proxy will flatter them; require the real MM-GBSA on summer).
**Predicted borderline/fail delta:** N5 (charge only ~50% at 7.4).
**Predicted FAIL by design (controls working):** NC1 (buried cation → affinity ≫ −8), NC2 (no warhead → affinity ≫ −8). If either passes, the gate/prep is broken.

Top 3 to advance: **N1, N2, N4.**
